summary: The unified engine is built, tested and selectable. It is not yet the default: LAZY_INTEL_ENGINE must be set to `unified`. Rollback is unsetting that variable, which needs no state migration because the two readers share one derived-state owner.

legacy.selector: LAZY_INTEL_ENGINE unset or any value other than `unified`
legacy.transport: zg and codegraph CLI subprocesses plus an externally provisioned Serena MCP server over stdio
legacy.evidence_quality: retrieval and graph results arrive as formatted text and are preserved as opaque blocks; no locator may be derived from them

unified.transport: long-lived private worker processes loading the vendored fork libraries over a Node IPC channel
unified.evidence_quality: retrieval, graph and semantic results carry canonical anchors with UTF-8 byte spans and the backend's own native id

state_compatibility.derived_indexes: Unchanged. Both readers call ensureIndexes in src/index-manager.js, so .zvec-grep/ and .codegraph/ keep the same layout, the same owner and the same leases. Switching modes migrates nothing and invalidates nothing.
state_compatibility.new_state: packages/core/src/workspace writes under a .lazy-intel state root. Nothing on the default query path writes there yet; it is exercised by test/contracts/workspace-scope.test.js and test/faults/publication.test.js.
state_compatibility.external_backends: In unified mode the external `zg`, `codegraph` and `serena` executables are not invoked on the query path. They remain installed and are still used by the legacy reader, which is what makes rollback instant.

procedure: Unset LAZY_INTEL_ENGINE (or set it to `legacy`) and restart the MCP server.
No index rebuild, no state deletion and no downgrade of a database is required.
Confirm with `node src/cli.js doctor`: the `engine` row reports the active mode and the legacy rows reappear.
rollback.verified_by: scripts/verify-release.mjs gate `rollback-switch`, which asserts the selector resolves to `legacy` when unset and `unified` when set.

not_yet_migrated: The unified reader is not the default. Flipping the default is a separate, deliberate release decision.
The workspace publication layer is implemented and tested but is not yet the gate in front of the derived indexes; the index-manager still owns readiness.
Single-parse convergence is enabled only for the languages in docs/unified/parser-convergence.json with `converged: true`. Every other language keeps its existing extractor.
Semantic reads cover `symbol` and `references`. `implementations` and `diagnostics` return unsupported_capability rather than a substituted answer.
